title: Sanitize user-controlled rule labels before using them as metric label values
answers: Why does the plugin origin metric show garbage/control characters?
How do I safely expose an alert rule label as a Prometheus metric label?
grafana_alerting_plugin_origin_rules has weird or oversized origin values
__grafana_origin label is not validated, can it break metrics?
body:
Symptom: grafana_alerting_plugin_origin_rules{origin=...} can contain control characters, CRLF, or very long strings because the value comes straight from the rule's __grafana_origin label.
Root cause: pkg/services/ngalert/models.PluginGrafanaOriginLabel (__grafana_origin) is never checked against LabelsUserCannotSpecify, so any caller with rule-write permission can set it to arbitrary text, and pkg/services/ngalert/schedule/metrics.go:updateRulesMetrics previously read it unmodified.
Fix pattern: before using an unvalidated, user/plugin-controlled label as a metric label (or HTTP header) value, strip ASCII control chars and cap the byte length via util.SanitizeControlChars.
Constraints: applies to any rule/annotation label not covered by LabelsUserCannotSpecify that ends up as a metric label, log field, or header; does not apply to labels already validated at write time.
applies: ngalert: any place a rule/plugin-supplied label value is turned into a metric label, header, or other exposed field
says: Why does the plugin origin metric show garbled control characters?
Alert rule labels expose weird characters when used in metrics
How do I safely expose an alert rule label as a metric label?
Plugin origin field contains control characters breaking metrics
Long or malformed strings appear in the plugin origin metric value
search: Rule label sanitization for metric labels and headers: before using any rule or plugin-controlled label (such as __grafana_origin) as a metric label value or HTTP header, strip ASCII and Unicode control characters and cap byte length via pkg/util/strings.go:SanitizeControlChars. Applies to labels not covered by LabelsUserCannotSpecify; does not apply to labels already validated at write time. Prevents control characters and CRLF injection in grafana_alerting_plugin_origin_rules and other exposed fields. Used in pkg/services/ngalert/schedule/metrics.go:sanitizePluginOriginLabel, sanitizeHeaderValue, updateRulesMetrics, and pkg/services/ngalert/eval/eval.go.
